2677.subject: Chemistry
2677.text: How many tripeptides can be prepared by linking the amino acids glycine, alanine and phenyl alanine?
2677.sol: Tripeptides are amino acids polymers in which three individual amino acid units, called residues, are linked together by amide bonds. In these, an amine group from one residue forms an amide bond with the carboxyl group of a second residue, the amino group of the second forms an amide bond with the carboxyl group of the third. Therefore, glycine ( NH ₂- CH ₂- COOH ) ,alanine and phenyl alanine can be linked in six different ways.

A relation R is symmetric if (a, b) R (b, a) R . For all elements in R , (a, b) = (b, a) , so the condition holds trivially. Thus, the relation is symmetric. A relation R is transitive if (a, b) R and (b, c) R (a, c) R . Since the only pairs are of the form (a, a) , if (a, a) R and (a, a) R , then (a, a) R , which is true. Thus, the relation is transitive.

121789.subject: Botany
121789.text: How is the thallus of liverworts positioned relative to the substrate?
121789.sol: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, e.g., Marchantia. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate . The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures. 122124.sol: Zooidogamy is found in Cycas. It is a type of plant reproduction in which male gametes, called antherozoids, reach the female gametes, called archegonium, by swimming in a path of water. It is also found in algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and some gymnosperms.

122125.subject: Botany
122125.text: Which one is a parasitic alga?
122125.sol: Cephaleuros is a parasitic thalloid green alga. Its common name is red rust. This alga is parasitic on some important economic plants of the tropics and subtropics, e.g. tea, guava, mango, coffee, etc. It damages the area of algal growth on leaves or kills the new shoots or disfigure fruit.

122553.subject: Botany
122553.text: Match List I with List II regarding the status of the notochord in different animal groups. List I List II (A) Urochordata (I) Notochord extends from head to tail and is persistent throughout life (B) Cephalochordata (II) Notochord is present only in larval tail (C) Vertebrata (III) Notochord is absent (D) Non-chordata (IV) Notochord is replaced by a vertebral column in adults Choose the correct answer from the optio
122553.sol: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail (A-II). In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from head to tail and is persistent throughout their life (B-I). In Vertebrata, the notochord is present during the embryonic period and is later replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult (C-IV). In Non-chordates, the notochord is completely absent (D-III). Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III). Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

122900.sol: Reticulate venation has veinlets forming a network, parallel venation has veins running parallel, pinnate venation has primary veins branching out, and palmate venation has veins radiating from a central point.

123218.text: Unicellular root hair arises from which part of Dicot root?
123218.sol: The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. 123898.subject: Botany
123898.text: During which of the following stages of cell division do homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres?
123898.sol: In Anaphase I of meiosis, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In contrast, during Anaphase of mitosis and Anaphase II of meiosis, the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate and move towards opposite poles. Metaphase I involves the alignment of bivalents at the equatorial plate, not their separation. Answer: Anaphase I of meiosis

125843.subject: Botany
125843.text: What is the purpose of storing pollen grains in liquid nitrogen?
options: As pollen banks for crop breeding programs
125843.sol: When once they are shed, pollen grains have to land on the stigma before they lose viability if they have to bring about fertilisation. How long do you think the pollen grains retain viability? The period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable and to some extent depends on the prevailing temperature and humidity. In some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release, and in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae, they maintain viabil

126017.subject: Botany
126017.text: Identify and name w,x,y and z respectively
options: Scutellum, Shoot apex, Radicle, Root cap

126291.subject: Botany
126291.text: If the male gamete of an angiosperm contains 14 chromosomes, what will be the number of chromosomes in the aleurone layer and the integument of the ovule, respectively?
126291.sol: The male gamete is a haploid cell ( n ). It is given that n = 14 . The aleurone layer is the outermost proteinaceous layer of the endosperm. Since the endosperm in angiosperms is formed by triple fusion, the aleurone layer is triploid ( 3n ). Its chromosome number will be 3 14 = 42 . The integument is a maternal sporophytic tissue that surrounds the ovule, meaning it is diploid ( 2n ). Its chromosome number will be 2 14 = 28 . Thus, the chromosome numbers in the aleurone layer and the integument are 42 and 28 , res

126331.subject: Botany
126331.text: Which one of the following pairs of plant structures has haploid number of chromosomes?
options: Megaspore mother cell and antipodal cells
126331.sol: The egg cell is one of the haploid cell of egg apparatus present in the micropylar end of embryo sac in seeded plants. It is also called oosphere and represents the single female gamete of the embryo sac. Antipodal cells are the haploid cells, usually three in number, present in embryo sac at the opposite end of micropyle. Their function is unknown and at fertilization, they may disintegrate or multiply and enlarge.

126352.subject: Botany
126352.text: An irregular mode of reproduction resulting in the development of an embryo without fertilisation is called I. parthenogenesis II. apogamy III. sporophytic budding Select the correct answer using the code given below.
126352.sol: In parthenogenesis formation of fruit occurs without fertilisation. In apogamy haploid (n) vegetative cell forms embryo without gametogenesis and fertilisation. In sporophytic budding diploid (2n) vegetative cell forms embryo from bud by vegetative reproduction. Thus, all of these processes are irregular modes of reproduction.

126444.subject: Botany
126444.text: Why are lipids considered part of the macromolecular fraction?
options: Because they are not strictly macromolecules
Because they are small molecular weight compounds
Because they are found in the acid soluble pool
Because they form structures like cell membranes and other membranes which get separated along with the acid i
126444.sol: Lipids are indeed small molecular weight compounds and are present not only as such but also arranged into structures like cell membrane and other membranes. When we grind a tissue, we are disrupting the cell structure. Cell membrane and other membranes are broken into pieces, and form vesicles which are not water soluble. Therefore, these membrane fragments in the form of vesicles get separated along with the acid insoluble pool and hence in the macromolecular fraction . Lipids are not strictly macromolecules.

126829.subject: Botany
126829.text: Which of the following organic compounds is the main constituent of lecithin?
126829.sol: Phospholipids are main constituents of lecithin. These molecules are composed of choline and inositole. It is found in all living cells as a major component of cell membrane.

126865.subject: Botany
126865.text: A competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase is
126865.sol: Malonate competes with succinate for active sites of succinate dehydrogenase.

127038.subject: Botany
127038.text: Which gases are responsible for increasing the temperature of atmosphere?
options: CH ₄, CO ₂, ~N ₂ O
CH ₄, CO ₂, ~N ₂ O
NO ₂, H ₂ ~S , CO ₂
127038.sol: The gases which are transparent to solar radiation but retain and partially reflect back long wave heat radiations are called greenhouse gases (GHGs). The phenomenon is called greenhouse flux. Because of greenhouse flux, the mean annual temperature of earth is 15^ C . In its absence it will fall to -18^ C . Hence, greenhouse gases keep the earth warm and hospitable. The various greenhouse gases are CO ₂ (warming effect 60 % ), CH ₄ (effect 20 % ), chlorofluorocarbons or CFCs (14 %) and nitrous oxide ( N ₂ O , 6 % )

127397.subject: Botany
127397.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the four major causes (the 'Evil Quartet') responsible for the accelerated rates of species extinctions in the world?
127397.sol: The accelerated rates of species extinctions are largely due to human activities. The four major causes are collectively called the 'Evil Quartet': 1. Habitat loss and fragmentation 2. Over-exploitation 3. Alien species invasion 4. Co-extinction Endemism refers to species confined to a specific region and not found anywhere else. It is a key criterion for identifying biodiversity hotspots for conservation, not a cause of species extinction. Answer: Endemism

127401.subject: Botany
127401.text: Match List I with List II regarding biodiversity conservation strategies. List I List II A. Sacred groves I. Ex-situ conservation of threatened animals B. Wildlife safari parks II. In-situ conservation of ecosystems C. Seed banks III. Ex-situ conservation of plant genetics D. Biosphere reserves IV. In-situ conservation with cultural significance Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
127401.sol: Sacred groves are tracts of forest set aside due to religious and cultural traditions, representing an in-situ conservation strategy. Wildlife safari parks involve keeping animals in protected, enclosed environments outside their natural habitat, making them an ex-situ conservation method. Seed banks store seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants for long periods, which is an ex-situ conservation strategy. Biosphere reserves are large areas of natural habitat protected for the conservatio

127515.subject: Botany
127515.text: One out of the following is not responsible for biodiversity loss.
127515.sol: Ex-situ conservation is not responsible for biodiversity loss, rather it is a method of conservation of biodiversity. It conserves selected rare plants/animals in places outside their natural homes. Alien species invasion, co-extinction and deforestation result in extinction of many species and loss of biodiversity.

127519.subject: Botany
127519.text: Assertion : Now-a-days, the biodiversity is declining with an accelerated rate. Reason : Exotic species are considered to be a major cause of extinction of species.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
127519.sol: The world is facing accelerated rates of species extinctions, largely due to human interference. There are four major causes (i) habitat loss and fragmentation, (ii) overexploitation, (iii) alien species invasions and (iv) co-extinctions. Non-native of alien species are often introduced inadvertently for their economic and other uses. They often become invasive and drive away the local species. The exotic species are considered to be second major cause of extinction of species (the first being habitat destruction).

128189.subject: Zoology
128189.text: Identify the given diagram of tissue performing secretion and absorption.
128189.sol: The given figure is of simple cuboidal epithelium. The cells are cubical and more or less squarish in shape. In surface view, the cells appear polygonal. The nuclei are rounded and lie in the centre of the cells. The cuboidal epithelium is present in the small salivary and pancreatic ducts, thyroid follicles, parts of membranous labyrinth, etc.

128738.subject: Zoology
128738.text: Deficiency of vitamin- B ₁₂ causes
128738.sol: The deficiency (hypovitaminosis) of vitamin- B ₁₂ or cyanocobalamine causes pernicious anaemia, demyelination of nerve fibres and glossitis (inflammation of tongue).

128791.subject: Zoology
128791.text: What is the average number of leucocytes present in the blood of a healthy individual?
128791.sol: Leucocytes are also known as white blood cells (WBC) as they are colorless due to the lack of haemoglobin. They are nucleated and are relatively lesser in number which averages 6000-8000 mm–3 of blood . Leucocytes are generally short lived. We have two main categories of WBCs – granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and

129009.subject: Zoology
129009.text: Sino-atrial nodes are called the ____ of the heart.
129009.sol: Sino-atrial nodes are called the pacemaker of the heart

129374.subject: Zoology
129374.text: Choose the incorrect statement for autonomic nervous system.
options: Transmit impulse from CNS to involuntary organs
Consists of sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system
129374.sol: The autonomic neural system controls and coordinates involuntary activities of various organs. It transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles of the body. The autonomic neural system is further classified into sympathetic neural system and parasympathetic neural system.

129403.subject: Zoology
129403.text: Given below is a table comparing the effects of sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system for four feature (a-d) . Which one feature is correctly described?
129403.sol: Sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system are the parts of autonomic nervous system. Autonomic nervous system is a part of peripheral nervous system that supplies stimulation via motor nerves to the smooth and cardiac muscles (the involuntary muscles) and to the glands of the body. The activity of the ANS is controlled principally by the medulla oblongata and hypothalamus of brain. Sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system tend to work antagonistically on the same organ.

129564.subject: Zoology
129564.text: What is the average amount of urine excreted per day by an adult human?
129564.sol: Urine formed by the nephrons is ultimately carried to the urinary bladder where it is stored till a voluntary signal is given by the central nervous system (CNS). This signal is initiated by the stretching of the urinary bladder as it gets filled with urine. In response, the stretch receptors on the walls of the bladder send signals to the CNS. The CNS passes on motor messages to initiate the contraction of smooth muscles of the bladder and simultaneous relaxation of the urethral sphincter causing the release of ur

129763.subject: Zoology
129763.text: The net pressure gradient that causes the fluid to filter out of the glomeruli into the capsule is
129763.sol: Kidneys help in the formation of urine, from the blood flowing through glomerular capillaries. About 20 % of plasma fluid filters out into the Bowman's capsule through a thin glomerular-capsular membrane due to a net or effective filtration of about 10 to 15 mm Hg . So, the nearest option is (1).

130230.subject: Zoology
130230.text: What is the significance of the binding of calcium ions to a subunit of troponin in muscle contraction?
options: It leads to the binding of myosin to the actin filaments
It masks the active sites for myosin
It causes the release of ADP and Pi from myosin
130230.sol: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.When a neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction, it releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. The binding of calcium ions to a subunit of troponin causes the removal of the masking of the active sites for myosin . This a

130833.subject: Zoology
130833.text: What does the epididymis lead to?
130833.sol: The male sex accessory ducts include rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens. The seminiferous tubules of the testis open into the vasa efferentia through rete testis. The vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis located along the posterior surface of each testis. The epididymis leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder. It receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. These ducts store and transport

130910.subject: Zoology
130910.text: What is the main cause of menstrual flow in human females?
130910.sol: The menstrual flow results due to breakdown of endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels which forms liquid that comes out through vagina . Menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised. Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy. However, it may also be caused due to some other underlying causes like stress, poor health etc. The menstrual phase is followed by the follicular phase. During this phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow to become a fully mature Graafian fo

131134.subject: Zoology
131134.text: Event Outcome A. Sperm capacitation 1. Prevention of polyspermy B. Acrosome reaction 2. Enzymatic breakdown of zona pellucida C. Fusion of sperm and egg membranes 3. Sperm gains ability to fertilize the egg D. Cortical reaction 4. Completion of meiosis II in the egg
131134.sol: Sperm capacitation: Sperm gains the ability to fertilize the egg after undergoing physiological changes. Acrosome reaction: Enzymes are released to break down the zona pellucida surrounding the egg. Fusion of sperm and egg membranes: Triggers the completion of meiosis II in the egg. Cortical reaction: Prevents polyspermy by altering the egg's outer layer.

131447.subject: Zoology
131447.text: What is the type of bacteria used by Frederick Griffith in his experiments?
131447.sol: In 1928, Frederick Griffith, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia) , witnessed a miraculous transformation in the bacteria. During the course of his experiment, a living organism (bacteria) had changed in physical form. When Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) bacteria are grown on a culture plate, some produce smooth shiny colonies (S) while others produce rough colonies (R). This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, whil

131745.subject: Zoology
131745.text: What is the difference between repetitive DNA and satellite DNA?
options: The repetitive DNA is shorter while the satellite DNA is longer in length
The repetitive DNA are DNA sequences containing small segments repeated several times while the satellite DNA
The repetitive DNA is found in humans while the satellite DNA is found in Animals
131745.sol: The difference between repetitive DNA and satellite DNA is the repetitive DNA are DNA sequences containing small segments repeated several times while the satellite DNA are repetitive DNA sequences containing highly repetitive DNA

132048.subject: Zoology
132048.text: What did Mendel’s experiments allow him to set up?
options: A framework of the theory of evolution
A basic framework of rules governing inheritance
132048.sol: . His experiments had a large sampling size, which gave greater credibility to the data that he collected. Also, the confirmation of his inferences from experiments on successive generations of his test plants, proved that his results pointed to general rules of inheritance rather than being unsubstantiated ideas. Mendel investigated characters in the garden pea plant that were manifested as two opposing traits, e.g., tall or dwarf plants, yellow or green seeds. This allowed him to set up a basic framework of rules

132093.subject: Zoology
132093.text: Which plants are represented as the parental generation in the Punnett Square?
132093.sol: The Punnett Square shows the parental tall TT (male) and dwarf tt (female) plants, the gametes produced by them and, the F1 Tt progeny. The F1 plants of genotype Tt are self-pollinated. The symbols & and % are used to denote the female (eggs) and male (pollen) of the F1 generation, respectively. The F1 plant of the genotype Tt when self-pollinated, produces gametes of the genotype T and t in equal proportion

132243.subject: Zoology
132243.text: What type of mutations are caused by deletions and insertions of DNA base pairs?
132243.sol: In addition to the above, mutation also arise due to change in a single base pair of DNA. This is known as point mutation. A classical example of such a mutation is sickle cell anemia. Deletions and insertions of base pairs of DNA, causes frame-shift mutations (see Chapter 5). The mechanism of mutation is beyond the scope of this discussion, at this level. However, there are many chemical and physical factors that induce mutations. These are referred to as mutagens. UV radiations can cause mutations in organisms –

132544.subject: Zoology
132544.text: Barr body is missing in the female suffering from
132544.sol: In normal females, number of Barr bodies is one less than the number of X chromosomes. One Barr body means the female has two X chromosomes. Turner's syndrome (44+ X 0) is a genetic disorder that affects only females. In this condition, cells of the affected female possess only one X chromosome, instead of two. Due to the presence of only one X chromosome, no Barr body is present in females suffering from Turner's syndrome.

132696.subject: Zoology
132696.text: What does the change in moth populations before and after industrialization demonstrate?
options: The impact of climate on moth coloration
The effects of industrial pollution on natural selection
The irrelevance of industrialization to evolutionary processes
The role of genetic mutations in moth populations
132696.sol: The change in moth populations demonstrates how industrial pollution affected natural selection, leading to an increase in dark-winged moths due to changes in their environment .During post- industrialisation period, the tree trunks became dark due to industrial smoke and soots. Under this condition the white-winged moth did not survive due to predators, dark-winged or melanised moth survived. Before industrialisation set in, thick growth of almost white-coloured lichen covered the trees - in that background the wh

132975.subject: Zoology
132975.text: Which of the following statements is not true ?
options: Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy
Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
132975.sol: Convergent evolution is the independent evolution of similar features in different and un-related species. Homology is based on divergent evolution whereas analogy/analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution. Analogous organs have different structures, but they evolve for the same function and thus have similarity. For examples, the eye of the octopus and of mammals or the flippers of Penguins and Dolphins.

133270.subject: Zoology
133270.text: What is the main objective of prevention of AIDS?
133270.sol: AIDS is caused by the Human ImmunoDeficiency Virus (HIV).People who are at high risk of getting HIV infection include individuals with multiple sexual partners, drug addicts who take drugs intravenously, individuals who require repeated blood transfusions, and children born to an HIV-infected mother.The spread of HIV infection is due to conscious behavior patterns and not due to natural causes or poor monitoring. The main objective of prevention of AIDS is to reduce the spread of the disease as there is no cure for

133804.subject: Zoology
133804.text: is the effect of Bacillus thuringiensis on insect larvae?
options: It makes them more resistant to attack
133804.sol: An example of microbial biocontrol agents that can be introduced in order to control butterfly caterpillars is the bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis (often written as Bt). These are available in sachets as dried spores which are mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants such as brassicas and fruit trees, where these are eaten by the insect larvae. In the gut of the larvae, the toxin is released and the larvae get killed. The bacterial disease will kill the caterpillars, but leave other insects unharmed.

134042.subject: Zoology
134042.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134042.text: Which of the following is a correct match between crop, variety and resistance to diseases? array lll Crop & Variety & array l Resistance to diseases array array
options: Chilli Pusa swarnim Chilly mosaic virus
134042.sol: array lll Crop & Variety & array l Resistance to diseases array Wheat & Himgiri & array l Leaf and stripe rust, hill bunt array Brassica & Pusa swarnim & White rust Cowpea & Pusa komal & Bacterial blight Chilli & Pusa sadabahar & Chilly mosaic virus array

134757.subject: Zoology
134757.text: During the isolation of genetic material from a cell extract, it is necessary to remove other macromolecules to obtain purified DNA. Which of the following pairs of enzymes is specifically used to remove RNA and proteins, respectively, from the mixture?
134757.sol: During the isolation of DNA, the cell extract contains various macromolecules such as RNA, proteins, lipids, and polysaccharides. According to NCERT, RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease, whereas proteins can be removed by treatment with protease. This ensures that only purified DNA remains for the subsequent precipitation step. Using DNase would degrade the DNA itself, which is the desired genetic material. Cellulase is used to break down plant cell walls, and lipase is used for lipids, not for the pr

134762.subject: Zoology
134762.text: Read the following statements regarding plasmids: (A) They are extrachromosomal DNA molecules. (B) They can replicate autonomously independent of the control of chromosomal DNA. (C) They are typically single-stranded DNA molecules. (D) They are linear DNA molecules. How many of the above statements are correct?
134762.sol: Plasmids are small, circular, double-stranded, extrachromosomal DNA molecules found in bacteria and some other organisms. Statement (A) is correct as they are distinct from the main chromosomal DNA. Statement (B) is correct because they possess their own origin of replication (ori), allowing them to replicate autonomously independent of the chromosomal DNA. Statement (C) is incorrect because plasmids are double-stranded DNA molecules, not single-stranded. Statement (D) is incorrect because plasmids are circular DNA

134776.subject: Zoology
134776.text: Which of the following methods is specifically suited for introducing recombinant DNA into animal cells?
134776.sol: In microinjection, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell. Biolistics (or gene gun) is a method suitable for plant cells, where cells are bombarded with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA. Heat shock treatment is used to make bacterial cells competent to take up plasmids. Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants and is used as a vector to introduce DNA into plant cells, not animal cells. Answer: Microinjection

134845.subject: Zoology
134845.text: A foreign DNA fragment is successfully ligated into the pBR322 cloning vector at the Sal I restriction site. The resulting recombinant plasmids are then transformed into host E. coli cells. What will be the growth characteristics of these recombinant E. coli cells when plated on media containing different antibiotics?
options: They will grow on tetracycline-containing medium but fail to grow on ampicillin-containing medium.
They will grow on ampicillin-containing medium but fail to grow on tetracycline-containing medium.
They will grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline-containing media.
They will fail to grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline-containing media.
134845.sol: In the pBR322 cloning vector, the restriction site for the enzyme Sal I is located within the tetracycline resistance ( tet^R ) gene. When a foreign DNA fragment is ligated at the Sal I site, it causes insertional inactivation of the tet^R gene. As a result, the recombinant plasmid loses its resistance to tetracycline. However, the ampicillin resistance ( amp^R ) gene remains intact and functional. Therefore, the recombinant E. coli cells will be able to grow on an ampicillin-containing medium but will fail to grow

135215.subject: Zoology
135215.text: When does the growth rate of a population following the logistic model equal zero? The logistic model is given as dN/ dt = rN (1-N/K)
options: When N nears the carrying capacity of the habitat
When death rate is greater than birth rate
135215.sol: If both becomes equal ,then division of them becomes one A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity.

135353.subject: Zoology
135353.text: Read the following statements regarding the contributions of Prof. Ramdeo Misra: (A) He obtained his Ph.D. in ecology under Prof. W. H. Pearsall. (B) He established teaching and research in ecology at Banaras Hindu University. (C) He was honoured with the Sanjay Gandhi Award in Environment and Ecology. (D) His efforts led to the establishment of the National Committee for Environmental Planning and Coordination, whic
135353.sol: Statements (A), (B), and (C) are correct facts regarding Prof. Ramdeo Misra as mentioned in the introductory biography of Unit X in the NCERT textbook. Statement (D) is incorrect because his efforts led to the establishment of the National Committee for Environmental Planning and Coordination (1972), which paved the way for the establishment of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (1984), not the Ministry of Agriculture. Therefore, exactly three statements are correct. Answer: Only three

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fb2.subject: Biology
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fb2.text: In a particular strain of E. coli , a mutation occurs in the i gene such that the synthesized repressor protein completely loses its affinity for the operator region. Which of the following best describes the expression of the lac operon in this mutant strain?
options: Transcription of z, y and a genes will occur only when lactose is provided in the medium.
The operon will be transcribed continuously irrespective of the presence or absence of lactose.
The operon will remain permanently switched off even if the inducer is added.
Only the z gene will be transcribed while y and a genes will remain repressed.
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fb2.sol: The i gene of the lac operon codes for the repressor protein. Normally, this repressor binds to the operator region and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes ( z , y , and a ). In the given mutant strain, the repressor protein loses its affinity for the operator region. As a result, it can no longer bind to the operator to block transcription. Since the operator is never blocked by the repressor, RNA polymerase will continuously bind to the promoter and transcribe the structural genes. This

6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b8b.subject: Physics
6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b8b.text: An electric pump extracts 3000 litres of water from a well 15 m deep in 5 minutes. The useful power of the pump is : (Take g = 10 m/s ^2 and density of water = 1000 kg/m ^3 )

6a13e468688ac6d0667aad54.subject: Biology
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad54.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The first formed primary xylem elements are called metaxylem and the later formed primary xylem elements are called protoxylem. Statement II: In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad54.sol: Statement I is incorrect because the first formed primary xylem elements are called protoxylem and the later formed primary xylem elements are called metaxylem. Statement II is correct because in stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This condition is known as endarch. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct. Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

6a2109b4219e1ae5a17229c1.subject: Biology
6a2109b4219e1ae5a17229c1.text: Match List I with List II. List I List II A Homologous structures I Antibiotic-resistant bacteria B Analogous structures II Australian marsupials C Adaptive radiation III Sweet potato and potato D Anthropogenic action IV Vertebrate hearts and brains Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - IV, B - III, C - I, D - II
A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
6a2109b4219e1ae5a17229c1.sol: Homologous structures share a common ancestry but may perform different functions. Vertebrate hearts and brains are classic examples of homologous structures. Analogous structures have different evolutionary origins but perform similar functions. Sweet potato (a root modification) and potato (a stem modification) both store food, making them analogous structures. Adaptive radiation is the process where organisms diversify rapidly from an ancestral species into a multitude of new forms. Australian marsupials are a w

85653.subject: Biology
85653.text: Two spherical unicellular organisms, X and Y, have the same cytoplasmic composition, metabolic pathways, and live in identical nutrient-rich aerobic conditions. The diameters of X and Y are, respectively, 10 and 20 m . When nutrients are not limiting, the ratio of total oxygen consumption per hour per cell of organisms Y to X is:
85653.sol: The total oxygen consumption per cell, when nutrients and oxygen are not limiting, is directly proportional to the volume of the cell (amount of metabolically active cytoplasm). 95293.text: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: In spring season cambium is more active and produces a large quantity of xylem having vessels with wider lumen

In winter, the cambium is less active and forms less xylem elements having narrow vessels this is called autum
The spring wood is dark in colour and has lower density.
95293.sol: In spring season cambium is more active and produces large quantity of xylem having vessels with wider lumen. The wood formed during this season is called spring wood or early wood. In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels, and this wood is called autumn wood or late wood. The spring wood is lighter in colour and has a lower density whereas the autumn wood is darker and has a higher density.

306445.subject: Physics
306445.text: The anode of a thermionic diode is wired to the negative terminal of a battery, while the cathode is wired to the positive terminal.
options: A large current will flow through the diode from the cathode to the anode.
No appreciable current will flow through the diode.
A large current will flow through the diode from the anode to the cathode.
306445.sol: In a thermionic diode, the cathode emits electrons when heated. When the anode is connected to the negative terminal of the battery and the cathode to the positive terminal, the diode is reverse-biased. The negative potential of the anode repels the electrons emitted by the cathode, preventing them from reaching the anode. As a result, the circuit remains incomplete and no appreciable current flows through the diode.

6a7a1ff87e86f55357029619.text: A dichloro organic compound is known to contain exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule. When 0.075 g of this compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate in a Carius tube, it produces 0.1435 g of silver chloride ( AgCl ) precipitate. The molar mass of the organic compound is g mol ⁻¹ . (Given: Atomic masses of Ag = 108 u and Cl = 35.5 u )
6a7a1ff87e86f55357029619.sol: Molar mass of AgCl = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 g mol ⁻¹ Moles of AgCl formed = 0.1435 143.5 = 0.001 mol Moles of chlorine atoms in the sample = 0.001 mol Since each molecule of the organic compound contains 2 chlorine atoms, the moles of the organic compound will be half the moles of chlorine atoms. Moles of organic compound = 0.001 2 = 0.0005 mol Molar mass of the compound = Mass Moles = 0.075 0.0005 = 150 g mol ⁻¹ Answer: 150
